title: Valkyries vs Dream in WNBA Finals Game 4 LIVE: Highlights, score

 Cydney Henderson Heather Burns Meghan L. Hall Callie Fin USA TODAY Updated Oct. 24, 2026, 3:15 p.m. ET ATLANTA — The Golden State Valkyries may be down, but they're far from out.
 After dropping Game 3 of the WNBA Finals , 97-71 , on Oct. 21 to fall into a 2-1 hole against the Atlanta Dream , Gabby Williams said the Valkyries aren't panicking yet. Instead, she shared head coach Natalie Nakase's message to the team. "Remember how long of a series this is and just how we can bounce back," she recalled.
 Poor shooting and turnovers have plagued the Valkyries. Golden State conceded 22 points on 17 turnovers in Game 3, marking its second consecutive finals game with double-digit giveaways after surrendering 24 points off 19 turnovers in its Game 2 loss. The Valkyries' stout defense has also been "undisciplined," Tiffany Hayes said.
 "It's very uncharacteristic of us, but we know we're going to make mistakes," said Hayes, who finished Game 3 with 14 points and three rebounds. "We all just talk together after the game and let each other know that it's a series for a reason. We can adjust, but we have to do it now and we have to stay together to do it."
 GAME RECAP: Another Angel Reese double-double as Atlanta Dream take 2-1 lead WINNERS AND LOSERS: Angel Reese (again), Valkyries' turnovers key WNBA Finals Game 3 The Valkyries will look to end their two-game skid in Game 4 on Saturday, Oct. 22. They'll have to stop a red-hot Dream team that's turning in historic performances left and right. Angel Reese became the youngest player to record three straight double-doubles in the finals in Game 3, while Rhyne Howard also etched her name in the history books as the first player to record back-to-back games with five or more steals in the finals.
 Now, the Dream is two wins away from their first WNBA championship in franchise history.
 USA TODAY Sports is on the ground in Atlanta, providing live updates and highlights from Game 4. Here's everything you need to know before Saturday's tipoff at State Farm Arena:
 Stream the WNBA Finals on Sling TV 3:15 pm ET Share this update Kiah Stokes makes WNBA Finals history
 Callie Fin
 Golden State Vakyries center Kiah Stokes is up to three blocks. She also had three blocks in Game 3, making her the first player in WNBA Finals history to record more than two blocks in four consecutive games. Stokes also passes Sylvia Fowles and Brittney Griner for the most total blocks in a WNBA Finals.
 3:09 pm ET Share this update Allisha Gray picks up fifth foul
 Marcus D. Smith
 Dream guard Allisha Gray picked up her fifth personal foul of the contest with 8:09 left in the game while defending Valkyries forward Kayla Thornton, who scored a layup fighting through the contact.
 3:06 pm ET Share this update Q3: Valkyries 54, Dream 45
 Callie Fin
 Although the Dream won the third quarter 19-12, the Valkyries will carry their lead into the fourth quarter of what could be a pivotal game in this series.
 Gabby Williams and Tiffany Hayes had six points each in the third quarter. Williams is up to a game-high 17 points. Both teams are shooting under 30% from the field (Valkyries 25%, Dream 23.5%). The Valkyries held on
 Angel Reese is 1-of-5 from the field and only made one attempt in the third quarter.
 2:46 pm ET Share this update Valkyries timeout
 Callie Fin
 After a big time 3-pointer from Isobel Borlase to cut the Dream's deficit to six points, Natalie Nakase called a timeout to talk to her team. The Valkyries led by 16 entering this period.
 2:44 pm ET Share this update Natalie Nakase tech as momentum shifts
 Callie Fin
 Rhyne Howard scored a 3-point play amid a 14-4 run for the Dream and got the crowd back involved at State Farm Arena. Amid the celebration for that highlight, Natalie Nakase was hit with a tech as she took issue with the call on Cecilia Zandalasini. Howard made the technical free throw but missed the other.
 2:37 pm ET Share this update Kaila Charles, the agitator, pokes at Angel Reese
 Marcus D. Smith
 The Valkyries needed to make adjustments giving themselves a more physical presence against the Dream. Kaila Charles has responded in Game 4. She's being a pest, not letting Atlanta push Golden State around. In fact, Charles is the one doing the pushing, jawing and letting it be known the Valkyries aren't soft.
 Charles was called for a shooting foul with 7:39 left. After the call, there was a little extracurricular from Charles as she poked Reese back and forth, both Maryland natives. The two got to talking before they were separated.
 2:21 pm ET Share this update Natalie Nasake on Valkyries at the half
 Victoria Hernandez
 The Valkyries are 31-6 when leading at halftime, which is a promising stat for Golden State heading into the break with the largest halftime lead of the series.
 Head coach Natalie Nasake spoke on the NBC broadcast about how her team has rebounded after dropping Game 3 in Atlanta.
 “Finally they decided to fight, so it was really good that they showed up," she said. "They’re playing their hearts out and that’s what I love."
 She also spoke on defending Dream star Angel Reese, who has five turnovers.
 "It’s just team defense, the same thing," she said. "It’s the same game plan, it’s just now that we’re executing it.”
 2:19 pm ET Share this update Halftime: Valkyries 42, Dream 26
 Callie Fin
 This is a completely different Golden State team than we saw in Game 2. En route to the largest halftime lead of any team in this series, the Valkyries beat the Dream in points in the paint (24-14), fastbreak points (7-0) and second chance points (5-3).
 Most notably, the Dream have given up 14 turnovers (more than their eight made field goals) while the Valkyries have only given up four. Reese has five of the Dream's turnovers and four points. It was the lowest scoring half of the season for Atlanta.
 Gabby Williams has a game-high 11 points.
 2:07 pm ET Share this update Angel Reese in foul trouble
 Callie Fin
 After an offensive foul, the Queen of the South is up to three fouls before halftime. She's led the Dream with three straight double-doubles in these finals, and now could be limited down the stretch.
 2:02 pm ET Share this update Atlanta timeout amid another Valkyries run
 Callie Fin
 Dream coach Karl Smesko has seen enough. The Valkyries are on a 9-0 and have outscored the Dream 17-9 in the second quarter with 2:43 left until halftime. Can he settle his team and position them for a comeback entering halftime?
 1:53 pm ET Share this update Kaila Charles, Naz Hillmon chirp at each other
 Marcus D. Smith
 Game 4 is intense. The Valkyries, down 2-1, are not backing down. Golden State forward Kaila Charles and Dream forward Naz Hillmon were going at it in the second quarter.
 Charles fouled Hillman, who didn't take kindly to the contact and let Charles know. Charles responded with words of her own, but it was Hillmon who must've said something that caught the official's attention because she was assessed a technical foul for the verbal interaction at the 6:58-mark in the second quarter.
 Gabby Williams made the free throw and immediately after Hillmon was found cutting to the basket for an easy layup.
 1:50 pm ET Share this update Tiffany Hayes picks up third foul
 Cydney Henderson
 Several players are in foul trouble early. Valkyries guard Tiffany Hayes, who started for the Valkyries, picked up her third foul with 7:50 remaining in the second quarter. She’s not the only one. Dream guard Allisha Gray is playing with three fouls.
 1:49 pm ET Share this update Rhyne Howard breaks down Q1
 Callie Fin
 Rhyne Howard had to stop and take a breath while discussing the game on a TV interview.
 "They're just being aggressive, which we expected from them. Their backs are against the wall right now. But we have to come out and combat that. We can't be comfortable. We can't allow them to get what they're wanting to get," she said.
 Here's what she said about staying out of foul trouble: "We just have to make the game simple. Obviously they're being aggressive and trying to get to the line, we have to stay straight up and force them to get tough shots."
 1:44 pm ET Share this update End of Q1: Valkyries 16, Golden State 11
 Callie Fin
 The Golden State Valkyries held the Dream under their quarter scoring after in the first. Kaila Charles and Cecilia Zandalasini have five points each for Golden State.
 Rhyne Howard leads the Dream with five points.
 1:40 pm ET Share this update Valkyries lose challenge
 Callie Fin
 Golden State coach Natalie Nakase didn't think Cecilia Zadalasini's drive to the basket featured an offensive foul on Naz Hillmon. After the Valkyries initiated a challenge, the officials reviewed and stood by their call. In what could be a close game, the Valkyries are now down a timeout and will not have the ability to challenge for the rest of the game.
 1:34 pm ET Share this update Golden State pulls ahead early
 Callie Fin
 A 12-0 run just put the Valkyries up 14-7 with 2:09 left in the first quarter. 2026 Defensive Player of the Year Angel Reese notched an emphatic block on what would've been Gabby Williams' second layup in a minute. She's trying to keep her team in control.
 1:28 pm ET Share this update LSU, Kim Mulkey back Angel Reese
 Heather Burns
 1:27 pm ET Share this update Allisha Gray in foul trouble early
 Cydney Henderson
 Dream guard Allisha Gray is headed to the bench early after picking up her third foul with 6:19 remaining in the first quarter. She picked up two of those fouls in the span of seven seconds. Gray was called for a charge after colliding with Tiffany Hayes while driving to the basket. She then picked up a personal foul on the other side of the court seconds later. Isobel Borlase entered the game for Gray, wo has two points in four minutes. 
 1:25 pm ET Share this update Rhyne Howard shining on defense
 Callie Fin
 As the Dream start on a 7-2 run, Rhyne Howard is getting ready for another defensive clinic with a highlight block on Veronica Burton's layup — and she followed it up with a 3-pointer after an early scoring slump in these finals.
 Read more about Howard's defensive impact HERE .
 1:19 pm ET Share this update Valkyries starting lineup shift
 Callie Fin
 In a must-win situation, Golden State Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase made a shift to her opening rotation. Tiffany Hayes and Kaila Charles are in for Cecilia Zandalasini and Kayla Thornton.
 1:15 pm ET Share this update Game 4 of WNBA Finals tips off
 Callie Fin
 We are officially underway at State Farm Arena! With 8:04 to it's 2-0 for the Dream.
 1:07 pm ET Share this update Are any WNBA Finals players All-WNBA?
 Callie Fin
 It took some time, but we finally have the All-WNBA results. Spoiler alert: none of the players on the court today are on the first team. Atlanta Dream teammates Angel Reese and Rhyne Howard are both on the second team, though.
 Read the full story HERE .
 12:26 pm ET Share this update WNBA Finals today
 Heather Burns
 Game 4 between the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries begins at 1 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock. The Dream hold a 2-1 advantage in the best-of-seven series.
 12:23 pm ET Share this update Watch Angel Reese warm up
 Heather Burns
 12:12 pm ET Share this update Busy day for sports in the ATL
 Heather Burns
 The day kicks off with the Atlanta Dream's WNBA Finals at 1 p.m. ET at State Farm Arena, followed by Georgia Tech football at 3:30 p.m. at Bobby Dodd Stadium, Atlanta United soccer at 7:30 p.m. at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, and the Hawks' NBA home opener at 8:30 p.m.
 12:05 pm ET Share this update Angel Reese is silencing her critics
 Heather Burns
 Angel Reese’s success doesn’t come as a surprise to either of them but likely does for the suddenly quiet crowd of Reese detractors who criticized and mocked her before and after she was taken with the No. 7 overall pick in the 2024 draft. It’s hard to think of another athlete who has silenced their doubters as effectively as Reese.Michael Jordan, Tom Brady, Lionel Messi, LeBron James and Serena Williams all weaponized criticism to do what some said they couldn’t. All-time greats, who faced moments in their careers where critics declared them too small, too old, or incapable of winning on the biggest stage. The criticism was holistic for Reese, who has seemed to catch flak for every facet of her existence over the last few years.  Read more for Callie Fin. 
 11:47 am ET Share this update What time is WNBA Finals game today?
 Heather Burns
 The No. 2 seed Golden State Valkyries host the No. 4 seed Atlanta Dream in Game 4 of the WNBA Finals at 1 p.m. ET on Saturday, Oct. 24, at State Farm Arena in Atlanta.

 11:42 am ET Share this update Angel Reese in signature pink
 Heather Burns
 After putting up three straight double-doubles, Angel Reese arrives in a pinstripe look. Ready to get down to business.
 11:40 am ET Share this update Gabby Williams ready to work
 Heather Burns
 Valkyries leading scorer Gabby Williams arrives at State Farm with her game face on.
 11:38 am ET Share this update Gabby Williams explains team speech
 Heather Burns
   Golden State Valkyries guard Gabby Williams says she had to show a "different kind of fire" with her team after the Valkyries dropped consecutive games in the WNBA Finals .
 On Oct. 19, the Atlanta Dream evened the series with a 79-65 Game 2 victory. Then, in Game 3 on Oct. 21, the Dream outlasted the Valkyries with a 97-71 win. After Game 3, Williams, who is typically even keel, gave a passionate and animated speech to her teammates.
 "I've been a little bit too loose as a leader, and that's kind of where, especially coach (Natalie Nakase) has been pushing me. I think I've kind of been a little bit too much of 'It's alright. We'll figure it out. We're good. We're good. We're good,'" Williams said Friday ahead of Saturday's Game 4 at State Farm Arena (1 p.m. ET, NBC).
 Read more from Meghan L. Hall 
 11:29 am ET Share this update How many games in the WNBA Finals?
 Heather Burns
 The best-of-seven WNBA Finals features a 2-2-1-1-1 format for the second time in league history. The higher seed hosts Game 1 and Game 2 before the series shifts to the home of the lower seed for Game 3 and 4. The remaining games will alternate between the higher and lower seed until a team wins four games and is crowed champion. The 2026 WNBA Finals marks the second best-of-seven series iteration.
